areas.name: 5 Mile
areas.description: Great rock with a wide variety of problems right next to the road make 5 Mile one of the most popular areas in the canyon. Ever popular moderate offwidth, 'Big Mouth' can be found within a few feet of the road, with many quality slabs and juggy faces nearby. Plenty of quality intermediates like 'Surfboard', 'Green Face', 'Baldy' are all right there. Loads of advanced and elite variations cover the 'Mr. Smiley' face on the Split Boulder. 'Butt Trumpet' is a popular advanced line, and has several elite variations. The Golden zone to the east has several great advanced lines like 'Golden' and 'Mr. T' as well as the elite highball 'Kill it in the Evening' and smaller moderates scattered through the surrounding woods. The newer Sentinels Zone is home to elite line 'Omega Man' and lots of highball moderates and intermediates and projects though the trail system is less developed.
areas.access: From the roadside parking, cross the road and the Split Boulders are right there

areas.name: Blind Spot
areas.description: The Blind Spot is a lone boulder just off the road on the north side with a tight collection of excellent problems including the popular advanced line 'Blind Spot', along with well liked intermediates 'Slap Fight' and 'Blind Man's Campus'.
areas.access: Park on the side of the road near the boulder.

areas.name: Cabbage Patch
areas.description: The Cabbage Patch is one of the most accessible roadside areas in the canyon. Jack's Boulder just feet from parking is loaded with popular moderates like 'Jack's Slab' and intermediates like 'Fat Albert Gang' and 'Fungus' and the ever popular 'Double Dyno' is just up hill. The 'Dean Problem' and its harder variations on the back of Jack's are some of the most interesting shothole climbing in the canyon, and reach into the advanced range. To the west 'Tom's Problem' is a popular intermediate, and just above it the Bagins cave houses a myriad of popular advanced and elite variations. To the west the Tiger Snake has several worthy lines and the area uphill around the Monolith also has many good lines including the new 'Luke's Dyno'.
areas.access: Park by the side of the road on the north side. You'll see the Brake boulder and Jack's boulder right next to the parking pullout.

areas.name: Campus
areas.description: The Campus boulder has a few good problems that still go, but many of the best lines like 'The Butt' and 'Big Man on Campus' were half buried by a rockslide a few years back. Perhaps it can be recovered someday...
areas.access: Park on the south side of the road across from the boulder.

areas.name: Crescent Crack
areas.description: Crescent Crack is a small cluster of new boulders from a recent rock slide in December 2022 up by the cliffs between Secret Garden and Cabbage Patch. 'The Sauce' is a nice intermediate in the area surrounded by several other mederates and intermediates along with a few harder looking projects.
areas.access: Crescent Crack boulders are mostly new blocks up by the cliffs from a recent rockslide. There are two ways to get there. Either park at the Park n' Ride and walk through Secret Garden and take the left turn up the Alpine Loop Trail, or reach the same turn coming from Cabbage Patch. Follow the trail up hill and you'll reach the Crescent Crack area as you approach the cliffs.

areas.name: East Gate
areas.description: Though just yards away from The Gate, The East Gate wasn't developed until decades later in the 90's. It is packed with great problems on quality rock, but it is a little harder to navigate and less busy than it's more popular neighbor. 'Round Room' is really unique and one of the most popular intermediates in the canyon. Other popular intermediates include 'Anonymous Arete', 'Coffee Girl', 'Red Stain' and 'Hidden Arete'. There are plenty of good moderate slabs scattered around the area, along with more on the Icarus boulder, the Between Boulders, and 'Potty Mouth' crack is great. Selection gets thinner in the advanced range, but 'M&M Roof' is a popular line and the newer 'Sunrise Arete' high in the talus and 'Jameson Breakfast' out east in The Farm zone are both worth a visit. Elite potential can be found on undone projects including some near the parking lot and many more up in the newer areas.
areas.access: From the parking head up a short trail on the north east corner of the parking lot

areas.name: Everything
areas.description: The Everything area above The Parking Lot and Secret Garden is a bit of a hike, but explorers will be rewarded with some excellent problems and plenty of project potential. There are several unknown blocks with project potential on the way up the east side of Bong Eater. Chad's Cave, just northeast of Bong Eater houses loads of fun intermediate and advanced lines on steep and blocky Big Cottonwood style features. Continue up the gully to a nice new elite line 'Elevated Squeezing' and project potential on the nearby Samurai Slabs. At the top of the area is the Everything Boulder with several high quality Advanced and Elite problems on a tall slightly overhanging face with Big Cottonwood style rock. A few large boulders hide potential projects higher on the hill.
areas.access: From the parking lot head up hill onto the Alpine Bloc trail and follow it up to Bong Eater, the circle around below to the west to reach Chad's Cave. Continue uphill then cut East to get to Everything. Parts can be quite bushwhacky.

areas.name: Green A. Gully
areas.description: The Green Adjective Gully is a newer area up the hill to the east of The Gate. The huge boulders high in the talus are densely packed with excellent problems and lots of projects waiting to be done with expansive views of the canyon. The West Gate zone off the left side of the trail has great problems across the grades from silly moderate 'Far Away Horse' to new intermediate classic 'Knockin' Boots' and the more advanced 'Body Shop' and 'Enter the Brine'. Further up is the daring high ball 'Last First Crack' surrounded by more great problems and potential projects. High on the hill in the talus to the right elite lines can be found like 'Hour of Power', 'Mr. Peanut' and 'The Settlement' as well as loads of excellent intermediates like 'The Fin' and 'The Shield' along with advanced problems like 'Karate Chop Kid', 'Halcyon' and 'Naughty Neighbor'.
areas.access: Park at the Gate then head north west past the Standard Overhand and the Tower to reach a large talus field. West Gate is to the left, University is to the right. Continue on up the trail to reach the main Green A Boulders.

areas.name: Grit Mill
areas.description: The Grit Mill (Sometimes mistakenly called the Grist Mill) is a few boulders around the Grit Mill parking lot below the LDS church vault. All the boulders in the guide are on public land, but going above the higher road behind Golden plates is private property. The Vault Roof cluster visible from the parking lot holds a variety of fun moderates, intermediates and one advanced problem: 'The Vault Roof'. 'Lava tag' is a unique intermediate on the back side. The rest are fun moderates with a few getting pretty tall on the south side. the huge 'Golden Plates' boulder straight up from the parking lot has several highball slabs and a few intermediate problems around the back. Just above it to the northwest is an interesting cave called Davey Jone's Locker that houses a few problems and lots of potential variations. The 'Holy' boulder has two fun intermediates 'Holy' and 'Full Authority'. There is some project potential down by 'Beach Town' and up the gully above 'Gripsalot'.
areas.access: From the Grit Mill parking lot, you can see the Vault Roof up a small hill to the west, Golden Plates boulder in teh talus to the north, or head uphill behind the bathroom to an abandoned dirt road the leads east to Holy.

areas.name: Hidden Forest
areas.description: Hidden forest is a beautiful secluded area with an excellent handfull of classic boulders. Great rock quality is spread across a broad range of grades including the advanced sloper testpiece 'Duct Tape', great introductions to intermediate LCC with 'Dale's Arete' and 'Steve's Problem' and lovely moderates like 'Kate Moss'.
areas.access: From parking head down across the stream and follow a small trail through the reeds to reach the main quarry trail. Turn left and head up canyon for several minutes. After crossing a bridge and coming around a bend to the right, there will be trails on the south side that head up a small embankment into the Hidden Forest

areas.name: Highborn
areas.description: Developed by Landon Schoenmann, the Highborn boulder is a medium sized block resting high on the sloping cliffs to the south of the Parking Lot and Temple Quarry. There are only two lines on the block, but they are good quality and the view is phenomenal.
areas.access: From the Temple Quarry parking lot, look up hill to the south to spot Highborn on a grassy patch above some cliffs. To get there, cross the stream and head up the gully to the left / east of the boulder. May involve some bushwhacking and scrambling to reach the boulder.

areas.name: Hitch Hiker
areas.description: The Hitch Hiker area includes some great boulders to the west along the creek along with a string of smaller blocks to the east. Older favorites like the moderate Hitch Hiker slabs are joined by popular newcomers like 'Air Jordan' and 'Gone 'Til November'. Boulders in the creek bed are best climbed later in the Fall when the creek is low.
areas.access: From the Parking head up the road and see the Hitch Hiker Boulders off to your right.

areas.name: Jimbo Boulders
areas.description: The Jimbo Boulders, found by Jim, are in a secluded forest area to the east of the foot bridge with a few good blocks including the advanced testpiece slab 'Neurosis' V8 and several fun lines on the Ms. Smiley Boulder along with some potential for more lines on other small blocks in the talus above.
areas.access: From the parking head down the winding dirt road and cross the bridge. Jimbo Boulders can be found along the trail to the left / east. The last stretch into the Jimbo area can be a bit bushwhacky, but keep going and you'll find the boulders.

areas.name: Junkie Boulders
areas.description: Junkie Boulders have been around since the 90's, and while the area enjoys cooler temps and all day shade, it is lesser known and tends to be less crowded. With good moderate slabs, and well liked intermediates like 'Junkie Arete', and several notable intermediate and advanced lines on the Batman Boulder, along with elite new lines like 'Pain and Ankle' in the talus, it's worthy area to spend some time. There is still plenty of project potential in the talus as well as a few undone lines on the 'Trail of Fears' Boulder by the trail.
areas.access: From the parking head down the winding dirt road and cross the bridge. Junkie Boulders can be found along the trail to the right / west

areas.name: Last Boulders
areas.description: The Last Boulders are two smaller blocks near the White Pine Trailhead parking lot. No known lines on these, but a few beginner and intermediate problems look possible with a little work to clear debris from recent avalanches.
areas.access: Park on the south side of the road near the boulders.

areas.name: Lens Flare
areas.description: Lens Flare is a newly developed lone boulder on the north side of the creek across from the Junkie Boulders. Several popular intermediate lines can be found here including 'Lens Flare' and 'Red Shift'
areas.access: From the parking head down canyon along the road until parallel with the Boulder, then head down a drainage to reach it

areas.name: Lizard Head
areas.access: Park on the right just past the entrance to the LDS vault. Head uphill onthe trail just east of the road that goes up to the vault.

areas.name: Nowhere
areas.description: Way up above Green A. Gully there is a single problem that has been done traversing a long sideways boulder over a highball drop off.
areas.access: Park at the Gate and hike up through Green A. Gully past Ancestors and Victorete then keep going up the gully and head left as it opens up until you reach the boulder.

areas.name: Outer Canyon
areas.description: An expansive boulder covered hillside north west of the canyon entrance, Outer Canyon gets year round sun, so it's a good place for Winter climbing, and gets quite hot in the summer. Some of the rock can be rather chossy, but a few gems are worth the hike including the massive Golden Egg, crystal covered Gemstone, and the Feature covered Dice Cube. There are also several excellent kid friendly boulders like The Shard, and The Birth Mark. Ever wish you could bring pooch to LCC? You're in luck! Outer Canyon is also the only boulder area in Little Cottonwood where dogs are allowed. Some boulders are on private property, but Salt Lake City is OK with bouldering as long as people stay away from the clearly marked water tanks, control startion, and service road in the Shark Tooth and Pioneer sub areas.
areas.access: About a mile north west of the Little Cottonwood Park n' Ride, there is a dirt pullout on the east side of the road. Park here and head east up the trail at the south corner of the pullout to access the main boulders. The trail will head uphill for about an 8th of a mile to reach the Pioneer Boulders off to the left of the trail. Then the trail curves around to the south past the Golden Egg and onto The Shard and The Gemstone. To access The Dice Cube it is easier to hike along the dirt road heading south from the pullout until you reach the Meat Balls boulders, and head up the switchbacks from there.

areas.name: Parking Lot
areas.description: The Parking Lot has a handful of fun boulders within seconds of your car. The cluster around the Shothole Boulder near the entrance has a number of good moderate and intermediate lines as well as the new elite problem 'Criminology' and a handfull of potential projects. Another cluster can be found along the beginning of the trail up to Secret Garden including solid intermediate slab 'No Parking' and a handfull of advanced lines around 'Holy Hell' that deserve more traffic. The Bush boulder has several quality moderates along with some newer advanced variations.
areas.access: From the parking lot, the boulders are all around

areas.name: Riverside
areas.description: Just across the road from 5 Mile, Riverside is home to a wide variety of classic problems on both sides of the creek including the picturesque 'Blue Steel'. Many quality problems across the grade range can be found right by the road on the Syringe boulder with many fun moedrates and intermediates on the way down the trail and to the west. The Riverside boulder proper is home to classic advanced line 'Shivers' and intermediates 'Jim' and the classic LCC slab 'Feck'. Across the bridge behind 'Blue Steel' are the advanced classic 'The Buzz' and it's elite variations as well as "Alzheimer's' in the Buzz zone. Further west on teh Far Side boulder popular intermediate 'Seems Easy' can be found along with several good moderte face problems on the back, and nearby the advanced arete 'Surprise' and it's elite variations are well liked. Newer boulders up in the Expadition zone are mostly in the moderate and intermediate grades, but a hand full of harder problems like 'The Sorting Hat' and 'JRich' have been established. West world has a few good lines and several smaller blocks awaiting development.
areas.access: Head downhill from the roadside parking. There is a trail right by the Syringe Boulder to reach Riverside. Another trail further east goes directly down to the Bridge to reach the Buzz and Far Side

areas.name: Secret Garden
areas.access: From the parking lot take the trail in the corner to the left of the bathrooms. This will lead you up to the main pipeline trail where you can turn right into Secret Garden

areas.name: Shadows
areas.description: Shadows is a lone boulder recently developed with two good lines at the end of a nice hike.
areas.access: Park on the south side of the road just past a guard rail and work your way down the hill near the guard rail to reach the quarry trail below. Find a good place to cross the creek and there are some trails through a clearing on the other side leading into the woods where Shadows can be found in a gully.

areas.name: Snowbird North
areas.description: Snowbird North includes two fantastic boulders with great rock quality near the road. The first is the Inception boulder with loads of moderate slab problems on the north east side, some popular intermediates on the south side like 'Jansen's Problem', and loads of harder lines with variation in the cave on the west side like 'Inception' and 'Super Chunk'. Further up the trail is the Sam Trap Boulder with popular 'Dick Van Dyke' traverse, 'Ping' great slabs on the west side and the elite traverse 'Wheel of Snowbird'.
areas.access: Park on the south side of the road just before the concreate divider begins. The boulders are uphill to the north.

areas.name: Snowbird South
areas.description: The Snowbird boulders on the south side of the road have some nice rock with beautiful views. Most are moderate slabs with a few that are quite tall. The River boulder has several fun jug lines, and the Loner boulder above has some easy high balls. Watch out for stinging nettle, especially around the easy slab boulder by the road.
areas.access: Park on the south side of the road just before the concrete divider begins. The boulders are downhill in the meadow, and more are south across the creek.

areas.name: Swamp Thing
areas.description: The Swamp Thing area is on the north side of the creek across from Hidden Forest, and includes two undeveloped boulders waiting for some attention. Detox is a rounded bulge hidden near the road, while Swamp Thing is a slightly overhanging face down in the reeds by the creek.
areas.access: From the parking walk up the road until you see an old dirt road heading down to the right. Follow the road east until you are parallel with Swamp Thing, then do a little light bushwhacking into the woods on swampy soild to find it near the creek.

areas.name: Temple Quarry
areas.description: The Temple Quarry is a great place for kids and beginners with it's easy trails, good landings, and friendly boulders like the Dragon Egg right next to the parking lot. There are historical markers along the trail with some history about the Mormon Pioneers that quarried here for the Salt Lake Temple. While most of hte lines are in the moderate and intermediate range, there are a few good harder problems up on the Overlook Boulder up on teh south hill and the elite 'Sizzle Grips' just across the creek.
areas.access: From the parking lot, most of the boulders are downhill toward the stream with some others further east off the trail

areas.name: The 3rd Planet
areas.description: The 3rd Planet is a small cluster of boulders developed by Nikki Smith. Most of the established lines are moderate and intermediate, but a few harder projects are still waiting for FAs.

areas.name: The Gate
areas.description: The Gate area is one of where bouldering began in Little Cottonwood back in the 1960's. The 'Standard Overhang' is one of the most popular intermediates in the canyon along with several other nearby favorites like 'Surprise Ending', 'E.B.P.', 'Left Side Direct' and the goof 'Party Trick'. Some of the best moderates in the canyon can also be found here with the well known slabs on the west side of the Gate Boulder and Greasy variations on the neighboring Spinal Twist boulder as well as fun aretes and faces on the Tower Boulder. Advanced problems include 'Crystal Pinch', 'Superfly' and 'Barfly' on the Standard Overhang boulder. 'Spinal Twist' is an older elite problem put up by Chris Sharma, and there are loads of other elite variations on the Standard Overhang Boulder. The Banjo zone is less trafficed but has several great problems and a newer zone including several undone projects for the adventurer.
areas.access: From the parking head up a short trail in the north west corner of the parking lot

areas.name: The Gullies
areas.description: Situated between the Riverside Buzz zone, and The Swamp, the Gullies is a lesser known area with a handful of worthy lines developed and documented by Niki Smith, Jay Keener and Victor Copeland. Great moderates like 'Rough Cut' and 'Darth Moss' can be found higher up the gully along with potential intermediate classic 'Blood Diamond'. Nearby 'Brute Fracis' is a well liked advanced line, and a few more elite lines and projects can be found down lower on the Remainder and Funner boulders.
areas.access: Park the same as the Swamp, cross the creek by the Moon Rock, then head uphill on a trail that veers right to the west. After coming to the Funner Boulder, continue on up the hill to reach The Gullies.

areas.name: The Hill
areas.description: The Hill is a steep area of densely packed boulders with a few outlying areas on the edges. It is known for elite lines like 'Triple Threat', 'Sean John', and 'Dominatrix' but is also home to loads of easier high quality problems. There are excellent tall slabs and moderate lines throughout the area starting with some good problems on the Obelisk and Stick boulders right near the road. Several popular intermediate lines can be found on Tom's Wall along with many others spread around The Hill. 'Wormography' and 'H King' are two excellent advanced problems along with the harder 'Jumper', 'Loggerhead' to the east and the very exciting 'Holy Moly' high up on the cliff band. Due to its faint trails and steep complex layout The Hill is less traveled, and still holds many projects across the grades for those willing to venture...
areas.access: From the parking head across the street and east toward the Stick Boulder. There is a path into The Hill just before reaching the Stick Boulder.

areas.name: The Swamp
areas.description: The Swamp is a good collection of large boulders across the road south from The Gate that can be found along the quarry trail. Classic intermediates like 'The Big Guy', 'Don't Fall' and 'Pride' are joined by a long list of popular Elites like 'Confluence', 'Tiny', 'Alchemy', 'Dunks on Deck', 'Eclipse' and 'Transience'. Loads of tall moderate slabs are peppered through the area along with a great collection of advanced problems like 'Maisch Slab', 'Extreme Hammocking', 'Smells Like Font' and newer lines up in the Talus like 'Redheaded Ramblings' and 'Sticks and Stones' in the new East Swamp area. There are plenty of projects remaining to be done.
areas.access: From the parking head down to the creek. There are good place to cross the creek near the Moonrock, or further upstream by the Japanese Garden. In the Spring when the creek is too high, The Swamp can be reached by crossing the bridge in Riverside, and hiking east for a few minutes.

areas.name: Trench Warfare
areas.description: The Trench Warfare area is a densely packed cluster of enormous boulders high on the south side of the canyon across from Cabbage Patch and west of Wasatch Resort. This newer area has a few well known lines including the popular elite 'Red Letter Day' and several other good problems spanning the grades on the surrounding boulders. 'Blueberry' is an excellent advanced problem to try out, and 'Papa Bell's Arete' is a fun intermediate at the bottom of the zone. With loads of newer problems and plenty of project potential this beautiful area is worth getting to know.
areas.access: Parking is the same as Cabbage Patch, but cross the road and head downhill toward the stream. Cross the stream and climb up through the woods

areas.name: Valhalla
areas.description: Valhalla is a large area high above White Pine North. There are only a handful of established problems including the elite highball 'Legends Only' and the majestic intermediate arete 'Terminus'. There are dozens of other boulders scatted up the hill with lots of potential if you're willing to make the hike.
areas.access: Park in the White Pine parking on the north side of the road, then climb up the trail near the south end of the pullout. After reaching the Sky Boulder zone in the talus either head straight up to reach Terminus, or head up behind Mullet Master to get to One of the Ones. Head directly west over the ridge behind Mullet Master to reach Brown Sugar.

areas.name: Wasatch Resort
areas.description: The Wasatch Resort is an the most expansive area in the canyon with twice as many problems as most other areas. The beautiful tree covered south hill is heavily shaded and home to a huge collection of fantastic boulders. The main access point is just west of the last home in the Wasatch Resort neighborhood. The home owner at the west end of the neighborhood is friendly to climbers, but be respectful and don't enter their property. The boulders right next to their backyard are fine to climb on, just be respectful and don't make a lot of noise. The massive Wasatch Resort area can be divided up into three main vertical sections with the Water Tower areas on the east, Dean, Paul Bunyon, and Upper Wasatch areas in the middle and the Cube, Yukon and Battle Star areas to the west. The Water Tower areas are a bit of a hike, but many excellent problems make the trek worthwhile including classic intermediate 'Classic' and quality advanced lines like 'Beck Face'. A handful of elite problems like 'Muenster Cheese Squeeze' and 'The English Patient' are nearby. Higher on the hill and further east potential projects abound! Up the center areas there are lots of moderate problems with good landings near the bottom of the area with plenty of popular intermediates like 'Sad Face Clown', and 'Der Undergriff'. Higher on the hill 'Will's Face' is well liked as well as high balls 'Babe' and 'Prime Rib' high up by the cliffs. Elite lines and variations are all over including 'Muffler' and 'Rodeo Sloth'. On the west end of the Wasatch Resort the Cube boulder is home to some great slabs and a few harder problems. Further west is the very popular advanced line 'First Down' with more popular advanced high balls up hill in the Yukon zone like 'Ready to Die' and 'Big Baby Jesus' and the short but well liked 'Toolshed' and 'Mini-Maisch'. Throughout the west zones elite high ball lines can be found from top to bottom with quite a few new problems going up in recent years like 'Wind Waker', 'Belly Grip', 'Klondike' and 'High Horse'. Potential projects abound, especially up toward Battlestar. With so many great problems in such a beautiful area, Wasatch Resort is worth exploring!
areas.access: Park at the Grit Mill parking lot, then cross the road to the south. Find a trail next to the entry road for Wasatch Resort and follow it down toward the creek. Cross just west of the last house and head up the trails into Wasatch Resort Boulders. May not be crossable in the Spring. It is possible to cross the bridge in Riverside, and bushwhack in from the east, by the Surprise Boulder.

areas.name: Water Station
areas.description: A few small blocks along the creek by the water station.
areas.access: Park in the pull out and walk up the sides of the creek.

areas.name: White Pine Chutes North
areas.description: The north White Pine Chutes is a medium sized talus field with loads of tightly packed problems including several well liked lines from the lower east 'Rainbow Cave' up to popular intermediates 'Fat Lip' and 'Red Headed Stepchild' high in the talus, and several advanced lines on 'Chocolate Starfish' in the brush to the east.
areas.access: Park in a long pull out on the south side of the road then cross and head uphill on a steep trail. Chocolate Starfish will be up and right near the end of the Trail. There are several breaks heading out left into the Talus for the other boulders.

areas.name: White Pine Chutes South
areas.description: The south White Pine Chutes have a hand full of popular problems, mostly on the Year of the Lamb Boulder which houses a myriad of variations and eliminates including intermediate, advanced and elite level lines.
areas.access: Park in the long pull out on the south side of the road then find a trail near the east end of the pull out and follow it downhill to the south to find the boulders in the woods.

areas.name: White Pine North
areas.description: White Pine North has a great collection of beloved lines on excellent covered rock spanning a huge talus field that extends high into the Valhalla Area above. From popular moderate lines on the Ping Pong boulder and the intermediate 'Fortune Cookie' near the road, to more advanced favorites on the Head On Boulder in the central area and committing high balls at the top of the talus, White Pine North has something for everyone. Check out the newly documented Tingy Town area to the east developed years back by Sam Tingy which includes lots of nice moderate lines along with a few undone projects in hidden pits and caves.
areas.access: Park in the big pullout on the north side of the road and head straight into the woods to reach Ping Pong and Fortune Cookie. To reach the higher areas find a trail toward the east end of the parking lot and follow it up through the woods into the talus.

areas.name: White Pine South
areas.description: White Pine South is a sprawling talus high in the canyon with hundreds of great problems on quality patina'd rock including the beautiful moderate slabs on the Moose Boulder, and popular intermediate highball 'Mom' as well as the epic V16 cave 'Grand Illusion'. Other favorites include intermediates like 'Tequila Sunset', 'Blunder' and 'Ring Toss', Advanced lines like 'Stephan's Dihedral', 'Prowler', 'Matt's Roof' and 'Nest Egg' and loads of other elite lines like 'Euro Roof', 'Grand Illusion',  'Mangalyaan' and 'The Good Listener'. Along with all these favorites are plenty of potential problems scattered throughout the vast talus fields, just waiting to be climbed.
areas.access: Park on either side of the road and head south across the creek. There is usually a log or two for crossing the creek at various points toward the middle of the parking area. Crossing the creek can be difficult in the spring. A longer safer spring route can be taken by parking at the White Pine Trailhead to the east and crossing that bridge then bush whacking across the meadow into the Moose Boulder area.

areas.name: White Pine Trailhead
areas.description: White Pine Trailhead covers a wide swath of aspen forest scattered with a wide variety of boulders. The most popular are the L' Heritage (AKA Great Divide) and the Wire Trail (AKA Crimpin' Connies) with lots of great problems at all levels. Lesser known newer areas to the west include great lines like the intermediate 'Solar Power' as well as advanced problems like 'Finders Keepers' and 'Fern Gully Roof' with a few harder problems like 'Super Serious'. There is a fair bit of new problem potential up in the Ferngully area, though recent avalanches have left some debris that may need to be cleared.
areas.access: park at the White Pine Trailhead parking lot, or along the road just above it. Enter the woods to the east by the highway sign and find the trail to reach the Wire Trail and L' Heritage. To reach Fern Gully and Finders Keepers head to the west end of the area along the road and find a trail going uphill that leads to Bullwinkle and other boulders above.

problems.name: The Surfboard Problem
problems.description: Start with left arete of the serfboard feature and high right crimp on the face then climb the double arete trending around to the right

problems.name: Green Face
problems.description: Start on the undercling in the middle fo the face and climb up and left over the apex

problems.name: Smiley Right
problems.description: Start on crimps on the big sloper shelf then punch up and right to the rail and finish up jugs

problems.name: Mr. Smiley
problems.description: Start on crimps on the big sloper shelf then follow crimps trending up and left to the top

problems.name: Mr. Smiley Right Exit
problems.description: Start on crimps on the big sloper shelf then follow crimps up and left and climb up and right through a crimp rail and finish up jugs

problems.name: Big Mouth
problems.description: Climb the crack, many possible betas

problems.name: Baldy Left
problems.description: Start on the low rail on the right side of the arete and climb up the arete moving around the left side onto the rails then up the interesting mantle sequence onto the slab

problems.name: Caress Arete
problems.description: Climb the arete on the right side
